\section[vietato]{vietato — forbidden, not allowed}

\label{lesson:IT-C385-vietato}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for optional, then the Italian for the obligation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: vietato}
\textbf{vietato} — \textquotedblleft{}forbidden, not allowed\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
È vietato fumare in tutto l'edificio.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Smoking is forbidden in the whole building.}
\end{quote}

On signs: \emph{vietato l'ingresso} — no entry; \emph{vietato fumare} — no smoking.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{vietato} is the past participle of \emph{vietare} \textquotedblleft{}to forbid\textquotedblright{}, inherited from Latin \emph{vetāre} \textquotedblleft{}to forbid\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vietato}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vietato}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{vietato}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for optional, then the Italian for the obligation, then say \emph{vietato} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does vietato mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Forbidden, not allowed\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[proibire]{proibire — to ban, to prohibit}

\label{lesson:IT-C385-proibire}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the obligation, then the Italian for forbidden.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: proibire}
\textbf{proibire} — \textquotedblleft{}to ban, to prohibit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Il comune ha proibito le macchine in centro.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The town council has banned cars in the centre.}
\end{quote}

Conjugated with \emph{-isc-}: \emph{proibisco}. Stronger and more official than \emph{vietare}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{proibire} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{prohibēre} \textquotedblleft{}to hold back, to forbid\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), built from \emph{prō} \textquotedblleft{}before\textquotedblright{} and \emph{habēre} \textquotedblleft{}to hold\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{proibire}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{proibire}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{proibire}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the obligation, then the Italian for forbidden, then say \emph{proibire} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does proibire mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To ban, to prohibit\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[tollerare]{tollerare — to tolerate, to put up with}

\label{lesson:IT-C385-tollerare}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for forbidden, then the Italian for to ban.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: tollerare}
\textbf{tollerare} — \textquotedblleft{}to tolerate, to put up with\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Non tollero i ritardi.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I do not put up with lateness.}
\end{quote}

Stress: \emph{tòllero}. \emph{Non tollerare il caldo} — not to cope with the heat.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tollerare} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{tolerāre} \textquotedblleft{}to bear, to endure\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for forbidden, then the Italian for to ban, then say \emph{tollerare} again
\end{itemize}

\section[autorizzare]{autorizzare — to authorise, to allow officially}

\label{lesson:IT-C385-autorizzare}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to ban, then the Italian for to tolerate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: autorizzare}
\textbf{autorizzare} — \textquotedblleft{}to authorise, to allow officially\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Se il preside ci autorizza, facciamo la festa a scuola.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{If the head teacher authorises it, we will have the party at school.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Autorizzare qualcuno a fare qualcosa}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{autorizzare} was borrowed from French \emph{autoriser}, from Medieval Latin \emph{auctōrizāre} (EtymDB), built on Latin \emph{auctor} \textquotedblleft{}author, guarantor\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{augēre} \textquotedblleft{}to increase\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{autorizzare}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{autorizzare}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{autorizzare}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for to ban, then the Italian for to tolerate, then say \emph{autorizzare} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[l'autorizzazione]{l'autorizzazione — the authorisation, the permit}

\label{lesson:IT-C385-autorizzazione}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to tolerate, then the Italian for to authorise.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: l'autorizzazione}
\textbf{l'autorizzazione} — \textquotedblleft{}the authorisation, the permit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Senza autorizzazione non puoi entrare.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Without authorisation you cannot go in.}
\end{quote}

Built on \emph{autorizzare}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{autorizzazione} is built on \emph{autorizzare}, which was borrowed from French \emph{autoriser}, from Medieval Latin \emph{auctōrizāre} (EtymDB), on Latin \emph{auctor} \textquotedblleft{}guarantor\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
